events/736_qizhao/phases/0/narrative: Du Fu was born in 712 in Gongxian, Henan. His grandfather Du Shenyan was a famous poet of the early Tang. As a boy Du Fu set himself a rule: “Read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand miles.”
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/instruction: Click the things in the house to find out what the boy wants.
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/npcs/0/dialog: On the desk lie Du Shenyan's drafts — “Only a man far from home is startled when the season turns.”
Grandfather's poems are wide and open. Mine should be too.
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/npcs/1/dialog: Grandfather always said: read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand miles.
events/736_qizhao/phases/0/npcs/2/dialog: Zimei, reading again? They say the jinshi exam is on again this year.
I want to go out and see the world first.
events/736_qizhao/phases/1/transitionTex: In 735 Du Fu went to Luoyang to sit the jinshi exam…
events/736_qizhao/phases/1/announcement/: The list: Du Fu — not passed.
events/736_qizhao/phases/1/dufu_reaction: So I failed. The world is wide — is one list the whole of it?
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/title: The great journey through Qi and Zhao
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/travelNarrati: After failing, Du Fu set out from Luoyang and spent the next few years roaming Qi and Zhao.
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/instruction: Click each stop and hear what he says on the road.
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/waypoints/0/d: My father holds a post here. I'll see him first.
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/waypoints/1/d: What is Daizong like? Across Qi and Lu, green with no end…
events/736_qizhao/phases/2/waypoints/2/d: One day I will climb the highest peak, and see how small the mountains are!
(This is the moment Du Fu wrote “Gazing at the Peak.”)
events/736_qizhao/phases/3/poemContext: You are standing on the summit. The lines are almost out of you — put each word back into the right blank.
events/736_qizhao/phases/3/puzzle:
What is Daizong like? Across ___, green with no end.
Nature ___ every wonder here; ___ cut dusk from dawn.
Layered clouds ___ and stir my chest; I strain my eyes at birds coming home.
One day I will ___, and see ___.
events/736_qizhao/phases/4/transitionTex:
In five years
Du Fu crossed Qi, Zhao, Wu and Yue,
made bold friends, and set himself beside the great ministers of old.
events/736_qizhao/phases/4/dufu_reaction: Li Bai… I have read his poems for ten years. They say he is coming to Luoyang too.
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/0/explanation: Du Shenyan was one of the early Tang's “Four Friends of Letters.” Du Fu's gift for poetry ran in the family.
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/1/question: “One day I will climb the highest peak, and see how small the mountains are” — which mountain is this?
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/1/explanation: “Gazing at the Peak” is about Mount Tai, the Eastern Peak. “Daizong” is its old name.
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line from “Gazing at the Peak”:
“Nature gathered every wonder here; ____ cut dusk from dawn.”
quiz/736_qizhao/quizzes/2/explanation: Shade and sun cut dusk from dawn — one side of the mountain is bright, the other dark. That is how huge Mount Tai is.
events/744_libai/phases/0/title: A Luoyang Tavern · Hearing About Li Bai
events/744_libai/phases/0/narrative: Spring, 744. One name is running through every street in Luoyang — Li Bai.
events/744_libai/phases/0/instruction: Walk round the tavern. Listen to what people say about Li Bai.
events/744_libai/phases/0/npcs/0/dialogu: Heard the news? Li Bai's been given gold and sent away. He's out of Chang'an!
Given gold and sent away — it sounds fine. It means they got rid of him.
events/744_libai/phases/0/npcs/1/dialogu: That Li Bai — “when the emperor called he would not board the boat, and said he was the immortal of wine”?
Tsk. That kind isn't afraid to die.
events/744_libai/phases/0/npcs/2/dialogu: What will you have, sir? Grape wine, just in at the west market?
Li Bai? He was here two days ago. Drank three jugs and went, and left a poem to pay for it.
Li Bai's poem on the wall
“The good wine of Lanling smells of saffron; poured into a jade bowl, it shines like amber…”
events/744_libai/phases/0/npcs/3/dialogu: Li Bai… I have been reading his poems for ten years.
If I could see him just once…
events/744_libai/phases/1/narrative: Round the corner, a middle-aged man in a white fur coat, a long sword at his belt, sits on a donkey with his head thrown back, laughing.
events/744_libai/phases/1/question: How do you speak to him?
events/744_libai/phases/1/options/0/text: “Du Fu of Gong county, styled Zimei. I have long admired you, Master Li Bai.”
events/744_libai/phases/1/options/0/resp: Ha! Zimei? I've read that line of yours — “I will climb to the very top and see how small the mountains are.”
events/744_libai/phases/1/options/1/text: “Master Li Bai! Will you drink a cup with me?”
events/744_libai/phases/1/options/1/resp: Perfect! We're the same kind of man. No need to be polite.
events/744_libai/phases/1/options/2/resp: In the moment they passed each other, Du Fu had a thousand things to say, and could not say one of them.
events/744_libai/phases/1/conclusion/nar: They took to each other at once. Spring, 744, in Luoyang. From then on people said the two names together: Li and Du.
events/744_libai/phases/2/narrative: Autumn. The three of them set out together through Liang, Song, Qi and Lu. Li Bai is going to look for immortals and the Way. Gao Shi came to find an old friend. Du Fu only wants to hold on to these days.
events/744_libai/phases/2/instruction: Move between the fields and the drinking table. Listen to them talk.
events/744_libai/phases/2/npcs/0/dialogu: “Drunk in autumn we sleep under one quilt; by day we walk hand in hand” — now that is living free!
Zimei, you hold yourself in too tight. Take off this skin — underneath, who isn't from heaven?
From here I go on to Qi and Lu, to see a Daoist master and be made a Daoist myself.
events/744_libai/phases/2/npcs/1/dialogu: Li Bai gets wilder every year.
Zimei, you are not like him. You have the people in your heart.
I mean to go to the frontier and join the army. Writing can't save the world.
events/744_libai/phases/2/npcs/2/dialogu: The three of them stop at a bare mound. No stone. No name.
Some lord. No telling which dynasty.
events/744_libai/phases/2/npcs/3/dialogu: Lord Li writes fine lines; often they sound like Yin Keng.
I am a traveller at Dongmeng too; I care for you like a brother.
events/744_libai/phases/3/narrative:
Li Bai is going on to Wu and Yue. Gao Shi has already gone south. Only Du Fu is left to see him off.
Li Bai: “Don't act like a child. While the poems are here, this is no parting.”
events/744_libai/phases/3/options/0/resp:
Autumn comes, and we look at each other still blown about like loose grass; the elixir is not made, and I am ashamed before Ge Hong…
(After he finished this poem, “To Li Bai,” Li Bai sent back one line only: “At Duling there is a man in plain clothes; the older he grows, the clumsier his mind.”)
events/744_libai/phases/3/options/1/text: Ask him to stay in Luoyang
events/744_libai/phases/3/options/1/resp: (throws his head back and laughs) He does not belong to one city.
events/744_libai/phases/3/options/2/resp: He goes off free and easy. I don't need to cry either.
events/744_libai/phases/3/conclusion/nar: After this parting the two never met again. But for the rest of his life Du Fu wrote more than ten poems about Li Bai.
events/744_libai/phases/4/transitionText:
Autumn, 745.
Du Fu goes west to Chang'an.
He will not leave for ten years.
events/744_libai/phases/4/dufu_reaction/: I should be going too. Chang'an…
quiz/744_libai/quizzes/0/question: In 744, in which city did Du Fu first meet Li Bai?
quiz/744_libai/quizzes/0/explanation: In the spring of 744 Li Bai, just “given gold and sent away” from Chang'an, came to Luoyang and met Du Fu. The two took to each other at once.
quiz/744_libai/quizzes/1/question: Who was the third poet travelling with Du Fu and Li Bai through Liang and Song?
quiz/744_libai/quizzes/1/explanation: In the autumn of 744 Du Fu, Li Bai and Gao Shi travelled together through Liang and Song (around Kaifeng and Shangqiu in Henan today). They climbed the Chuitai terrace and hunted at Mengzhu marsh. It became one of the famous stories of Chinese literature.
quiz/744_libai/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line from Du Fu's “Thinking of Li Bai on a Spring Day”:
“Bai's poems have no rival; his thoughts ___ free, like no one else's”
quiz/744_libai/quizzes/2/explanation: “Bai's poems have no rival; his thoughts float free, like no one else's.” Du Fu wrote more than ten poems about Li Bai in his life, and this is one of the most famous things he ever said in praise of him.
events/747_exam/phases/0/narrative: In 747 the emperor ordered a special exam. Anyone who “masters one art” could come to Chang'an and sit it. Du Fu came full of hope.
events/747_exam/phases/0/instruction: Click the people around you and talk to them about this special exam.
events/747_exam/phases/0/npcs/0/dialogue: They just held an exam. Why another one this autumn?
events/747_exam/phases/0/npcs/1/dialogue: Usually it's school students and men sent up from the provinces. This time all sorts of odd talents have come.
events/747_exam/phases/0/npcs/2/dialogue: In my day you waited your turn for a post. The special exam puts you straight in, above your rank!
events/747_exam/phases/0/npcs/3/dialogue: Half of them got in by begging for a recommendation. It spoils the name of scholars. An honest man is ashamed to stand with them.
events/747_exam/phases/0/npcs/4/dialogue: A special exam is luck, not something you can ask for! The last one was 742 — five years ago!
events/747_exam/phases/0/npcs/5/dialogue: They say the emperor has called a special exam. Anyone with one skill may sit it.
events/747_exam/phases/0/nextTrigger/lab: Enter the palace for the exam
events/747_exam/phases/0/triggers/0/labe: Enter the palace for the exam
events/747_exam/phases/1/narrative: Du Fu straightened his robe and cap and walked into the solemn exam hall.
events/747_exam/phases/1/instruction: Click Li Linfu to hear how the exam will run.
events/747_exam/phases/1/npcs/0/dialogue: His Majesty wishes to gather every talent under heaven. All who master even one art are ordered to Chang'an.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/0/que: One exam subject is called “Old Tunes of the Airs and Odes.” The Airs of the States and the Greater and Lesser Odes come from which book?
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/0/exp: The “Airs and Odes” are the Airs of the States and the Greater and Lesser Odes in the Book of Songs, the earliest collection of Chinese poetry.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/1/que: Who wrote the earliest surviving five-character poem by a named poet?
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/1/exp: Ban Gu's “On History” is taken as the earliest surviving five-character poem by a named poet.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/2/que: The Music Bureau was enlarged and given the job of setting music for the state sacrifices. When did that happen?
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/2/exp: Under Emperor Wu of the Han the Music Bureau was greatly enlarged. It collected folk songs and set the music for the state sacrifices.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/3/que: Which of these is not a common ending for a yuefu poem's title?
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/3/exp: Yuefu titles commonly end in ge (song), xing (ballad), yin (prelude), qu (tune) and the like. Xu (preface) is not one of them.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/4/que: Which statement about yuefu poems and old-style poems is right?
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/4/opt: Yuefu poems are one kind of old-style poem
Old-style poems and yuefu poems both come with a tune
Yuefu poems mostly speak of feelings, old-style poems mostly tell stories
The poems of the New Yuefu movement are really old-style poems, not yuefu
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/4/exp: Yuefu poems belong to the old-style poems. An old-style poem does not need a tune, but yuefu were originally sung to music. The New Yuefu movement carried on the yuefu spirit, so its poems still count as yuefu.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/5/que:
Complete this line from Jia Yi's “Rhapsody on the Owl”:
“Heaven and earth are the furnace, the Maker is the smith; yin and yang are the coals, and all things are the ___”
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/5/exp: From Jia Yi's “Rhapsody on the Owl.” Heaven and earth are a furnace, nature the smith, yin and yang the coals, and all things the bronze being melted down — everything is always being made over again.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/7/que:
Complete this line from Yu Xin's “Lament for the South”:
“A straight rainbow ran through the ramparts, a comet came down to the ground. Where once a tiger crouched and a dragon coiled, add ___”
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/7/exp: From Yu Xin's “Lament for the South.” Jinling once looked like a crouching tiger and a coiled dragon, a seat for emperors, and over it the yellow banners and purple air of a Son of Heaven.
events/747_exam/phases/4/narrative: Du Fu decided to ask around Chang'an and find out what really happened at this exam.
events/747_exam/phases/4/instruction: Talk to people, gather clues, and work out the truth about the exam.
events/747_exam/phases/4/npcs/0/dialogue: Very few passed this special exam.
events/747_exam/phases/4/npcs/1/dialogue: I hear that this year the local offices sifted the papers first, and only then sent them up to the Department of State Affairs.
events/747_exam/phases/4/npcs/2/dialogue: Everyone staying with us is a commoner's son. Not one of them passed.
events/747_exam/phases/4/npcs/3/dialogue: A pity. I was just short.
Xue Ju? Zhang She? Aren't they already officials at court?
That doesn't stop them sitting the special exam.
events/747_exam/phases/4/npcs/4/dialogue: The chief minister, Li Linfu, Duke of Jin, thought too many men from the fields had come, and feared they would let out the secrets of the court… — Yuan Jie
events/747_exam/phases/5/narrative: Du Fu thought for a long time. He put all the clues together and made up his mind about this exam…
events/747_exam/phases/5/question: What do you think is the real reason he failed?
events/747_exam/phases/5/options/0/respo:
Ah, what a shame.
Still, it feels like I am missing something.
events/747_exam/phases/5/options/1/respo:
In the whole exam, not one commoner passed!
That cannot be right.
Everything points the same way: Li Linfu staged it, so he could say “no talent is left in the fields.”
Only then can he block honest words and keep the emperor in the dark.
And there is nothing I can do about it.
events/747_exam/phases/5/conclusion/narr: Du Fu finally understood: the exam was a trick from the start. The chief minister Li Linfu wanted to hold on to his power and feared new men would threaten him, so he reported to Emperor Xuanzong that “no talent is left in the fields,” and made up a result in which nobody passed. That year not one candidate was taken. Du Fu's dream of serving at court was over.
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/0/question: Why did Du Fu fail the exam?
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/0/options/1: Li Linfu rigged the exam and said “no talent is left in the fields”
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/0/options/2: He did not sit the exam
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/0/options/3: He was ill and missed it
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/0/explanation: In 747 the powerful minister Li Linfu rigged the exam to stop new talent rising up against him. He reported to Emperor Xuanzong that “no talent is left in the fields,” and not one candidate was taken.
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/1/question: Which great poet became Du Fu's friend around his Chang'an years?
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/1/explanation: Du Fu met Li Bai at Luoyang in 744. They travelled together afterwards and became close friends. Du Fu wrote many poems remembering Li Bai.
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/2/question:
Complete Du Fu's famous line:
“Read ten thousand scrolls to pieces, and you ____ as if a god were moving your hand”
quiz/747_exam/quizzes/2/explanation: Read ten thousand scrolls to pieces, and you write as if a god were moving your hand — read widely, and the words come of themselves.
events/751_lifu/phases/0/title: The streets of Chang'an · Eve of the rites
events/751_lifu/phases/0/narrative: In 751 Emperor Xuanzong will perform the three great rites — the offering at the Taiqing Palace, the offering at the ancestral temple, the sacrifice at the southern altar. All Chang'an is celebrating, hung with lanterns and streamers.
events/751_lifu/phases/0/instruction: Talk to people in the street about the ceremony, and about the chance to “present a poem.”
events/751_lifu/phases/0/npcs/0/dialogue: Word is the emperor will hold the three great rites. The whole court is run ragged.
events/751_lifu/phases/0/npcs/1/dialogue: An offering at the Taiqing Palace, an offering at the ancestral temple, and a sacrifice to Heaven at the southern altar.
A ceremony like that comes barely once in ten years.
events/751_lifu/phases/0/npcs/2/dialogue: The price of paper has gone up all over Chang'an.
Those scholars are all up half the night writing poems.
events/751_lifu/phases/0/npcs/3/dialogue: If your writing catches the emperor's eye, you could rise in a single step.
events/751_lifu/phases/0/npcs/4/dialogue: Only, this business of presenting poems—
Are you presenting writing, or praise for the emperor?
events/751_lifu/phases/0/npcs/5/dialogue: Chang'an has never been short of men who can write.
is someone who can make the emperor look.
events/751_lifu/phases/1/narrative: Late at night. The oil lamp burns small as a bean. Ruined drafts and an empty wine jug lie scattered on the desk.
events/751_lifu/phases/1/instruction: Click the desk, the crumpled paper and Du Fu to see how things stand.
events/751_lifu/phases/1/npcs/0/dialogue: The ink is still wet. The paper says—
events/751_lifu/phases/1/npcs/1/dialogue: You pick up a balled-up draft—
(Every line crossed out and written over.)
events/751_lifu/phases/1/npcs/2/dialogue: But if I don't, how will the world ever hear my voice?
events/751_lifu/phases/2/title: Taking up the brush · Sliding puzzle
events/751_lifu/phases/2/narrative: Under the lamp Du Fu picks up his brush — lines from the three poems churn in his head. Put them back together.
events/751_lifu/phases/3/title: The palace gate · Presenting the poems
events/751_lifu/phases/3/narrative: Outside the palace gate, students crowd in, every one of them here for the petition box.
events/751_lifu/phases/3/instruction: Talk to the students at the gate and see how presenting a poem works.
events/751_lifu/phases/3/npcs/0/dialogue: They say the petition box opens today.
events/751_lifu/phases/3/npcs/1/dialogue: If the emperor picks you out, your whole life changes.
events/751_lifu/phases/3/npcs/2/dialogue: His Majesty wishes to seek out every writer of talent in the empire.
If a man has real ability, the court will not let him go to waste.
events/751_lifu/phases/4/announcement/te: The Emperor found them remarkable. He is to wait at the Academy for orders, and be tested on his writing.
events/751_lifu/phases/5/narrative: Time passes. Nothing follows. In Chang'an, people are still talking about it.
events/751_lifu/phases/5/instruction: Walk the streets of Chang'an at night and hear what people say.
events/751_lifu/phases/5/npcs/0/dialogue: I hear Du Fu's been kept on at the Academy.
events/751_lifu/phases/5/npcs/1/dialogue: So he'll be an official soon, then?
events/751_lifu/phases/5/npcs/2/dialogue: That only means—they let him go on waiting.
events/751_lifu/phases/6/transitionText:
Night.
Du Fu stands in a street in Chang'an.
Far off, the palace blazes with light.
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/0/question: In 751, which work won Du Fu the notice of Emperor Xuanzong?
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/0/explanation: In the first month of 751 Xuanzong held three great ceremonies: at the Taiqing Palace, at the ancestral temple, and to Heaven and Earth. Du Fu sent in the Three Rites Poems. The emperor read them, found them remarkable, and told him to wait at the Academy for orders.
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/1/question: After the poems won him notice, what did Du Fu actually get?
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/1/options/1: A wait at the Academy and a place on the candidate list — and then nothing
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/1/explanation: “Summoned for a test of his writing, handed over to the officials, placed on the list of candidates” — it sounds splendid. All it meant was that he was now eligible. Li Linfu still ran the tests, and Du Fu fell back into a long wait.
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in Du Fu's famous line about scraping by in Chang'an:
“At dawn I knock at rich men's gates, at dusk I follow the dust of ____.”
quiz/751_lifu/quizzes/2/explanation: “At dawn I knock at rich men's gates, at dusk I follow the dust of fat horses. Leftover wine, cold scraps — a hidden bitterness everywhere.” From “Twenty-two Rhymes Presented to Assistant Director Wei,” about ten years of living off others in the capital.
events/755_anshi/title: The An Lushan Rebellion Breaks Out
events/755_anshi/phases/0/narrative: The tenth month of 755. Chang'an. After ten years stuck in the capital, Du Fu's post has finally come.
events/755_anshi/phases/0/instruction: Look at the appointment letter on the desk.
events/755_anshi/phases/0/npcs/0/dialogu: A decree with a red seal lies open on the desk — “Du Fu is appointed sheriff of Hexi.”
Four years of waiting, and the court has finally given me a post.
Sheriff of Hexi? A ninth-rank nobody who chases bandits?
events/755_anshi/phases/1/narrative: Du Fu lifts his brush to write back. But what should he say?
events/755_anshi/phases/1/question: How should Du Fu turn the post down?
events/755_anshi/phases/1/options/0/text: “I will not be sheriff of Hexi — bending my back for it is too bleak.”
events/755_anshi/phases/1/options/0/resp: Those are my own words. Sheriff of Hexi — I won't go.
events/755_anshi/phases/1/options/1/text: “How can I bow and scrape to serve the powerful, and never once show a happy face?”
events/755_anshi/phases/1/options/1/resp: (pause) …Those are Li Bai's lines, not mine.
events/755_anshi/phases/1/options/2/text: “No talent, so the wise ruler casts me off; too often ill, so old friends drift away.”
events/755_anshi/phases/1/options/2/resp: (pause) …Those are Meng Haoran's lines. I have words of my own.
events/755_anshi/phases/1/conclusion/nar: Du Fu sends up a polite refusal. At court the water stirs again.
events/755_anshi/phases/2/transitionText: A few days later, the Department of State. A letter of refusal lies on the desk.
events/755_anshi/phases/2/announcement/t: Du Fu is reassigned as armory officer in the Crown Prince's guard.
events/755_anshi/phases/2/dufu_reaction/: Looking after weapons… all right. Better than sheriff of Hexi.
events/755_anshi/phases/3/narrative: The eleventh month of 755, Chang'an. A dispatch comes galloping down the post road from the north.
events/755_anshi/phases/3/instruction: Click the people around you and hear how they say it: “An Lushan has rebelled.”
events/755_anshi/phases/3/npcs/0/dialogu: Fanyang — the army has risen at Fanyang! An Lushan has rebelled!
Every town on the road folds at the sight of them. Nobody can stop them!
events/755_anshi/phases/3/npcs/1/dialogu: Nonsense! The Emperor is at the Huaqing pools, and General An is his adopted son. Why would he rebel?
Have you been at the wine, spreading wild reports?
events/755_anshi/phases/3/npcs/2/dialogu: A post rider wouldn't dare make it up…
But if it is true — the whole land is going to come apart.
events/755_anshi/phases/3/npcs/3/dialogu: Go, tell the Chief Minister at once!
Not a word of this! Not a word!
events/755_anshi/phases/3/npcs/4/dialogu: “Anyone who speaks of the rebellion is to be beheaded.”
events/755_anshi/phases/4/transitionText:
The sixth month of 756.
Tongguan Pass is lost.
Emperor Xuanzong flees for Shu in the night.
Chang'an has no ruler.
events/755_anshi/phases/4/announcement/t: “The imperial carriage goes west to Shu. I will share these hard days with all my people.” — imperial decree
events/755_anshi/phases/4/dufu_reaction/: I settled my family in Fuzhou, and I cannot get out of Chang'an myself.
events/755_anshi/phases/5/narrative: The rebels are in the city. Broken walls, soldiers running loose. Not one guard left.
events/755_anshi/phases/5/instruction: Walk through the fallen city. Remember everything you see.
events/755_anshi/phases/5/npcs/0/dialogu: Our son — the rebels took him away!
He is only sixteen. He is only sixteen!
events/755_anshi/phases/5/npcs/1/dialogu: Even the Emperor has run. Where are we supposed to go?
…One more day alive, then. That is all.
events/755_anshi/phases/5/npcs/2/dialogu: Everyone still in this city belongs to us now!
Anyone who dares leave is cut down.
events/755_anshi/phases/5/npcs/3/dialogu: Someone has cut these words at the foot of the wall: “The country is broken; the hills and rivers remain. Spring in the city, and the grass grows deep.”
…Those are the words in my own heart.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/narrative: Du Fu stands on the wall of Chang'an, looking out at the broken palace.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/instruction: Seven of Du Fu's worries are hidden in the picture — click them and hear the lines he writes
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/0/text: The beacon fires have hung by the clouds a long time; since the rebel horsemen came they have never gone out.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/1/text: The spring blossom of my old country knows nothing; this spring it opens as bright as ever.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/2/text: The houses of Chang'an are still standing; where has the Emperor's carriage gone?
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/3/text: The city has fallen and the days are bleak; the broken wall stands there, empty.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/4/text: I want to ask how it is at home in Fuzhou; alone in the western capital, there is no way to know.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/5/text: Their screeching falls in with the battle music; their crying still carries the sound of weeping blood.
events/755_anshi/phases/6/points/6/text: Only fallen petals reddening the pool; whose tears ran all night long?
events/755_anshi/phases/6/progressivePoe: The country is broken; the hills and rivers remain. Spring in the city, and the grass grows deep.
Moved by the times, the flowers spill tears; grieving at parting, the birds startle my heart.
The beacon fires have burned three months on end; a letter from home is worth ten thousand in gold.
I scratch my white head and the hair grows thinner; soon it will not hold a hairpin at all.
events/755_anshi/phases/7/title: Getting Out · The Wards of Chang'an
events/755_anshi/phases/7/narrative: Cross the grid of Chang'an's streets, keep clear of the rebel patrols, and leave by the Jinguang Gate.
events/755_anshi/phases/7/conclusion: In the fourth month of 757, Du Fu went out by the Jinguang Gate on the west side of Chang'an and made for Fengxiang.
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/0/question: Who started the An Lushan rebellion?
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/0/explanation: In the winter of 755 An Lushan, who held three military commands at once, raised his army at Fanyang, saying he came to “clear the Emperor's side and punish Yang Guozhong.” Shi Siming was one of his commanders — hence the name, the An Lushan rebellion.
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/1/question: What was happening when “Spring View” was written?
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/1/options/0: Du Fu was climbing Mount Tai
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/1/options/1: Du Fu was trapped in fallen Chang'an
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/1/options/2: Du Fu was at the thatched cottage in Chengdu
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/1/options/3: Du Fu was drifting in Kuizhou
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/1/explanation: After Chang'an fell in 756, Du Fu was caught by the rebels on his way to join Emperor Suzong and taken back to the city. In the spring of 757, looking at the broken capital, he wrote “Spring View.”
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line from “Spring View”:
“Moved by the times, the flowers spill tears; grieving at parting, the ____ startle my heart.”
quiz/755_anshi/quizzes/2/explanation: “The country is broken; the hills and rivers remain. Spring in the city, and the grass grows deep. Moved by the times, the flowers spill tears; grieving at parting, the birds startle my heart.” — bright spring carrying grief: the land is the same, everything human is gone.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/0/travelNarra: Fourth month, 757. In rags, Du Fu went out of Chang'an by the west Jinguang Gate and crossed the rebel lines.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/0/instruction: Click each stop and see how Du Fu got down this dangerous road.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/0/waypoints/0: I have to be out the Jinguang Gate before dark.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/0/waypoints/1: Sir, the rebels are thick up ahead. You still mean to go to Fengxiang? It's far too dangerous!
Emperor Suzong has taken the throne at Fengxiang. I am only a man in plain clothes, but I can still serve my country!
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/0/waypoints/2: Cross the water. Shoes already torn through.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/0/waypoints/3: Fourth month, 757. Du Fu walked into Fengxiang in rags.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/1/transitionT: Suzong saw him — “straw sandals before the Son of Heaven, both elbows out through the sleeves” — was moved by such loyalty, and made him Reminder of the Left.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/1/announcemen: “Du Fu is appointed Reminder of the Left.” — decree of Emperor Suzong
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/1/dufu_reacti: Your servant… will not fail to speak.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/2/narrative: Less than a month into the job, Chancellor Fang Guan was stripped of his office after losing the battle at Chentao. A memorial demanding his punishment has already gone up.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/2/instruction: Find out how the Fang Guan case came about, then decide whether to save him.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/2/npcs/0/dial: Chancellor Fang lost badly. Two thousand ox-carts. The whole army gone.
But a general who loses a battle is not punished hard — that is the custom.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/2/npcs/1/dial: Fang Guan took the enemy lightly and pushed on. He threw away an army and shamed the country. He must be punished hard.
The emperor is in a rage. Whoever begs for him is one of his party.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/2/npcs/2/dial: “Fang Guan is a bungler. He lost thousands of men. Put him to death by law, and answer to the empire.”
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/2/npcs/3/dial: Zimei, you have only just taken the post. Stay out of this.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/3/narrative: A blank sheet of paper lies open on the desk.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/3/question: Will you send up a memorial to save Fang Guan?
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/3/options/0/r: A Reminder of the Left is for exactly this.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/3/options/1/r:
…I can't.
(But then this post would not be a Reminder's any more.)
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/4/transitionT:
The memorial went up.
Emperor Suzong was furious.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/4/announcemen:
“Du Fu is of his faction. Hand him to the three courts for questioning.” — decree of Emperor Suzong
(Zhang Hao fought for him: “Punish Du Fu and no one will ever speak up again.” So he was let go.)
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/4/dufu_reacti: Your servant will not defend himself. But everything he said was for the country.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/5/narrative: Suzong let Du Fu go home to Fuzhou. He had not seen his wife and children for a year.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/5/npcs/0/dial: (Her face is all tears. She cannot get out a word.)
We thought… we would never see you again.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/5/npcs/1/dial: The boy does not know him any more.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/5/npcs/2/dial: (The little girl holds on to Du Fu's leg and will not let go.)
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/5/npcs/3/dial: My wife and children stare, as if I should not be here; when the shock passes they are still wiping their eyes.
The little ones will not leave my knees — afraid I will go away again. …I have been gone too long.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/6/transitionT:
In the ninth month of 757 the Tang army took back Chang'an.
In the eleventh month Du Fu rode back to the capital with the emperor.
events/757_zuoshiyi/phases/6/dufu_reacti: This post… do I go on with it…
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/0/question: Who started the An Lushan rebellion?
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/0/explanation: The rebellion is named after An Lushan and Shi Siming, who led it one after the other. It is the point where the Tang turned from its height into decline.
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/1/question: What post was Du Fu given during the An Lushan rebellion?
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/1/explanation: A Reminder of the Left was there to tell the emperor when he was wrong. That is why Du Fu is called “Du the Reminder.”
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line from “Spring View”:
“Beacon fires have burned three months on end; one ____ from home is worth ten thousand in gold.”
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/2/explanation: The war went on and on. One letter from home was worth more than ten thousand in gold — that is how much he missed his family.
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/3/question: Put these events of the An Lushan rebellion in order
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/3/items/0: An Lushan raises his army at Fanyang
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/3/items/2: Du Fu makes his way to Fengxiang
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/3/items/3: Du Fu is made Reminder of the Left
quiz/757_zuoshiyi/quizzes/3/explanation: 755 An Lushan raises his army → 756 Chang'an falls → Du Fu risks the road to Fengxiang → Emperor Suzong makes him Reminder of the Left.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/0/narrative: Summer 759. A great drought in Huazhou. Du Fu was a junior officer there — in charge of sacrifices, ceremonies and schools.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/0/instruction: Get on with your work in the office — you will soon find you can't.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/0/npcs/0/dialo: Sir, another draft order has come in from the front.
The army lost at Yecheng. The court wants more men from the counties near the capital.
This time they are taking old men too.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/0/npcs/2/dialo: The sheets are covered in small writing: “draft rolls,” “grain demands,” “reports of farmers who have vanished.”
If I don't write poems, I will go mad.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/2/narrative:
At dusk I stopped at Shihao village. By night the officers came to seize men.
There is a noise in the dark.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/2/instruction: Click the picture. Watch it one panel at a time.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/3/narrative: Du Fu came back to Huazhou. The desk was piled with draft orders. One brush. One blank sheet.
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/0/question: What does “The Officer at Shihao” record Du Fu seeing the night he stayed in Shihao village?
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/0/options/1: Officers seizing men at night; an old woman going in her husband's place
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/0/options/2: Rebel troops killing everyone in the village
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/0/explanation: “At dusk I stopped at Shihao village. By night the officers came to seize men. The old man climbed the wall and ran; the old woman went to the door.” — Two of her three sons were already dead in the war. In the end she was taken away herself, to cook for the army. It is the bitterest poem in the Three Officers and the Three Partings.
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/1/question: After Du Fu gave up his post in 759, where did he take his family first?
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/1/explanation: In the early autumn of 759 Du Fu resigned his post at Huazhou and took his family west to Qinzhou (Tianshui in Gansu today), then on through Tonggu into Shu. That was the end of his official career, and the start of the wandering that filled the rest of his life.
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the opening of “The Officer at Shihao”:
“At dusk I stopped at Shihao village. By night the officers came to ____ men.”
quiz/759_qinzhou/quizzes/2/explanation: “At dusk I stopped at Shihao village. By night the officers came to seize men.” — Two lines in, and the suffering of ordinary people in the An Lushan rebellion is already right in front of you.
events/760_caotang/phases/0/narrative: Spring 760. Huanhua Creek, west of Chengdu.
events/760_caotang/phases/0/instruction: Walk along the creek and decide where to build the cottage.
events/760_caotang/phases/0/npcs/0/dialo: Bamboo leaves, clean wind. A man could live here.
events/760_caotang/phases/0/npcs/1/dialo: Water enough. I can water a garden.
events/760_caotang/phases/0/npcs/2/dialo: A hundred-year nanmu — I could read in its shade.
events/760_caotang/phases/0/npcs/3/dialo: Zimei, my friend, I have had the timber sent over.
It is a plain little place, but it will keep the wind and rain off.
Anything you need, come to the governor's office.
events/760_caotang/phases/1/narrative: Late spring. The cottage is up.
events/760_caotang/phases/1/instruction: Click the four parts of the house, one by one, and settle in.
events/760_caotang/phases/1/npcs/0/dialo: Three layers of thatch. Enough to keep the sun off.
events/760_caotang/phases/1/npcs/1/dialo: Alders block the sun, their leaves singing in the wind. Bamboo in the mist, dew dripping from the tips.
events/760_caotang/phases/1/npcs/2/dialo: Growing herbs — that is the work of an official with no post.
events/760_caotang/phases/1/npcs/3/dialo: The clear river runs level, its banks almost gone. Quiet trees, and at evening, many flowers.
Here by Huanhua Creek, clear hills and clean water. At last I can stop moving.
events/760_caotang/phases/2/narrative: The cottage is finished. Old friends start to come.
events/760_caotang/phases/2/instruction: Talk to two of the guests.
events/760_caotang/phases/2/npcs/0/dialo: The court has called me to the capital. I don't know when we will meet again.
Take care, Zimei — if I am not in Chengdu, I am afraid…
events/760_caotang/phases/2/npcs/1/dialo: Zimei. Years, and no sight of you. That ride through Liang and Song feels like yesterday.
Li Bai… he died at Dangtu, the year before last.
events/760_caotang/phases/2/npcs/2/dialo: Guests again today, sir? I brought you some new wheat.
Old Cui on the south side says your poems have got all the way to Chang'an.
events/760_caotang/phases/2/npcs/3/dialo: Master Du! We are here to grab your thatch again!
events/760_caotang/phases/3/transitionTe:
Eighth month, high autumn — the wind howls,
and tears three layers of thatch off my roof.
The thatch flies over the river and scatters on the far bank,
the high pieces caught in the tops of the trees.
events/760_caotang/phases/3/announcement: “The boys of the south village know I am old and weak — they play the thief right in front of my face.”
events/760_caotang/phases/3/dufu_reactio: I come back, lean on my stick, and sigh.
events/760_caotang/phases/4/title: “My Thatched Roof Torn Apart by the Autumn Wind” · last stanza
events/760_caotang/phases/4/poemContext: Cold rain in the bed. The quilt is years old, cold as iron. And still a thought comes up in him — put each phrase back in the right blank.
events/760_caotang/phases/4/puzzle:
If only I had ___, to shelter ___!
In wind and rain, ___!
Oh! When will such a house rise before my eyes? Then let my own hut ___, and that is enough!
events/760_caotang/phases/4/blanks/3: break alone and let me freeze
events/760_caotang/phases/4/distractors/: a boat safe on the river
events/760_caotang/phases/4/poemTitle: My Thatched Roof Torn Apart by the Autumn Wind (last stanza)
events/760_caotang/phases/5/transitionTe:
In 764 Yan Wu came back to govern Shu, and for a while Du Fu held a junior post in the Ministry of Works.
In 765 Yan Wu fell ill and died.
Du Fu had no one left to lean on. He took a boat east.
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/0/question: Which creek in Chengdu was Du Fu's thatched cottage built beside?
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/0/explanation: Du Fu's cottage stood beside Huanhua Creek in Chengdu. The site is now the Du Fu Thatched Cottage Museum.
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/1/question: “If only I had a thousand great houses” — what is Du Fu feeling here?
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/1/options/1: He worries about the country and its people, and wants every poor person to have a roof
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/1/options/2: He wants to build a palace
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/1/explanation: The autumn wind had just torn his own roof apart, and what he thought about was every poor person in the world. He would rather freeze himself, if only they had somewhere to live. That is a big heart.
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line:
“If only I had a thousand great houses, to shelter all the world's poor, ____!”
quiz/760_caotang/quizzes/2/explanation: To shelter all the world's poor, smiling — he wanted every poor person to have a roof, and something to smile about.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/0/travelNarrat: Autumn, 765. After Yan Wu died, Du Fu put his family on a boat and went east along the river, through the Three Gorges.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/0/instruction: Click each stop and hear him think out loud.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/0/waypoints/0/: At the mouth of the Qingyi I watch the tide rise. Where are you now? On what high terrace?
events/765_kuizhou/phases/0/waypoints/1/: Sick a long time now. I have stopped drinking. One more town where we live under someone else’s roof.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/0/waypoints/2/: A guest so long in the south. How could a man stay well?
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/narrative: Bai Maolin, the governor of Kuizhou, gave him a thatched house at Rangxi. Du Fu moved in. Autumn.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/instruction: Click what is outside the window and what is on the desk. Feel this autumn.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/npcs/0/dialo: Sharp wind, high sky, apes wailing. Clear shoal, white sand, birds circling back.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/npcs/1/dialo: Endless falling leaves come rustling down. The endless river comes rolling on.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/npcs/2/dialo: Worn down, I have just set down my cup of cloudy wine.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/npcs/3/dialo: Sir, Governor Bai sent someone with today’s charcoal.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/1/npcs/4/dialo: Hardship and bitterness, frost thick in my hair…
events/765_kuizhou/phases/2/poemContext: The ninth day of the ninth month. One man. One terrace. A whole river of wind. Put the lines back where they belong — later readers called this the finest seven-character poem ever written.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/2/puzzle:
Sharp wind, ___. Clear shoal, ___.
Endless falling leaves ___. The endless river ___.
Ten thousand miles, ___. A hundred years, ___.
Hardship and bitterness, ___. Worn down, I have just set down ___.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/2/distractors/: green grass, an old friend coming
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/title: Autumn Meditations · Images in the Mind
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/narrative: That year Du Fu wrote “Eight Autumn Meditations,” “Thoughts on Ancient Sites” and “Five Poems on the Generals,” one after another. Every one of them is a poem about politics in disguise.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/instruction: Listen to at least two of these poems.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/npcs/0/dialo: Jade dew has withered the maple woods. Over Wu Mountain and the Wu Gorge the air turns cold and dark.
(Looking north to Chang’an — the farther I get from it, the more it looks like a dream.)
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/npcs/1/dialo: A thousand hills and valleys run down to Jingmen. The village where Zhaojun grew up is still there.
(Zhaojun was sent far from home too. So was I.)
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/npcs/2/dialo: Duke Han built the three forts to keep the northern riders out and raise our banners there.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/3/npcs/3/dialo: An old cypress stands before Kongming’s temple, branches like bronze, roots like stone.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/4/transitionTe:
In the first month of 768,
Du Fu finally decided to leave the gorges and take a boat east.
events/765_kuizhou/phases/4/dufu_reactio: However wide the world is, I still have to walk a little more of it.
quiz/765_kuizhou/quizzes/0/question: About how many poems did Du Fu write while he was in Kuizhou?
quiz/765_kuizhou/quizzes/0/explanation: In under two years at Kuizhou, Du Fu wrote about 430 poems — nearly a third of everything of his that survives. It was the most productive time of his life.
quiz/765_kuizhou/quizzes/1/question: What have later readers called “Climbing High”?
quiz/765_kuizhou/quizzes/1/explanation: The Ming critic Hu Yinglin called “Climbing High” the finest seven-character regulated poem of all time. All eight lines are matched pairs, and it holds a whole world in it.
quiz/765_kuizhou/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the missing word from “Climbing High”:
“Endless falling leaves come rustling down, the endless river comes ____ on”
quiz/765_kuizhou/quizzes/2/explanation: Endless falling leaves come rustling down, the endless river comes rolling on — leaves everywhere in the air, the river rolling east and never stopping. Huge, and sad.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/0/transitio:
Spring, 768.
Du Fu takes his family out through the Three Gorges.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/0/dufu_reac: Where do we go now? We can't go home again.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/1/narrative: Winter, 768. Du Fu finally climbs the Yueyang Tower he has heard about for years.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/1/instructi: Look out from the tower — four directions, four feelings.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/2/travelNar: 769 to 770. Du Fu and his family drift between Tanzhou, Hengzhou and Leiyang.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/2/waypoints: No relative will take us in. We tie up the boat at Jiangling.
Ah! What road is left to put this body on?
The year ends, every grass is dead; a hard wind splits the high ridge.
Old and sick, with one lone boat.
(Floodwater blocks the boat. It stops at the Fangtian post station. The county magistrate sends wine and meat.)
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/3/narrative: Moored for the night. Mist rises off the river. Du Fu falls asleep in the cabin and dreams of the old days.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/3/instructi: Click the shadows floating on the river.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/3/panels/1/: Brother Zimei, the thatched cottage is still standing.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/3/panels/3/: Zimei, I read your poems. Ten years now.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/3/panels/5/: (Laughter comes through the mist — or maybe there is nobody there at all.)
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/4/transitio:
Winter, 770.
Going from Tanzhou to Yueyang.
A flood on the way; the boat is stuck at the Fangtian post station for days.
The county magistrate sends wine and meat.
Du Fu is 59. He can no longer get up.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/4/announcem: In the winter of 770 Du Fu died on a boat going from Tanzhou to Yueyang, aged 59.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/4/dufu_reac: The blood of war still runs, the noise of armies has not stopped…
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/5/transitio:
43 years later, in 813.
His grandson Du Siye carried the coffin home to be buried at Yanshi, and passing through Jingzhou he asked Yuan Zhen to write the epitaph.
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/5/announcem: “Zimei reaches up to the old Songs and the Li Sao, and takes in Shen and Song below. His words outdo Su and Li; his breath swallows Cao and Liu… Since there have been poets, there has never been one like Zimei.” — Yuan Zhen
events/770_xiangjiang/phases/5/dufu_reac: (He got no fame while he lived. 1200 years after his death, he is the Sage of Poetry.)
quiz/770_xiangjiang/quizzes/0/question: How old was Du Fu when he died?
quiz/770_xiangjiang/quizzes/0/explanatio: Du Fu was born in 712 and died in 770, at the age of 59.
quiz/770_xiangjiang/quizzes/1/question: What did later ages call Du Fu?
quiz/770_xiangjiang/quizzes/1/explanatio: Du Fu was honoured as the “Sage of Poetry” for how much he cared about the country and its people, and for his skill in verse. His poems are called “history in verse.”
quiz/770_xiangjiang/quizzes/2/question:
Fill in the famous line from “Climbing the Yueyang Tower”:
“Wu and Chu are split apart to the southeast; ____ floats day and night”
quiz/770_xiangjiang/quizzes/2/explanatio: Wu and Chu are split apart to the southeast; heaven and earth float day and night — Lake Dongting is so wide that it seems to have cracked the land of Wu and Chu open, and heaven and earth bob in it day and night.
timeline/character/description: The greatest realist poet of the Tang. His name is said together with Li Bai's: “Li and Du”
timeline/stages/0/summary: Du Fu was born in Gong County, Henan. As a young man he traveled to Luoyang and the old lands of Qi and Zhao, and met Li Bai.
timeline/stages/0/events/0/summary: Du Fu failed the exam on his first try, set off through Qi and Zhao, and left behind "Gazing at the Peak".
timeline/stages/0/events/1/summary: Du Fu met Li Bai in Luoyang. They became close friends and traveled together through Liang and Song.
timeline/stages/1/summary: Du Fu went to Chang'an to look for a post. He was stuck there ten years, saw how dark politics was, and gave in bit by bit.
timeline/stages/1/events/0/summary: Emperor Xuanzong held a special exam. Li Linfu staged the “no talent left out” trick, and nobody passed.
timeline/stages/1/events/1/summary: Du Fu offered Emperor Xuanzong three odes — "Offering at the Taiqing Palace", "Offering at the Ancestral Temple", "The Rite at the Southern Altar" — and was called in for a writing test.
timeline/stages/2/summary: The An Lushan rebellion broke out. The golden age collapsed. Du Fu was driven from place to place, and his hopes of office died.
timeline/stages/2/events/0/summary: An Lushan rose in arms against the Tang. Chang'an fell, and Du Fu was trapped by the rebel army.
timeline/stages/2/events/1/state: Close to the center of power at last
timeline/stages/2/events/1/summary: Du Fu escaped from fallen Chang'an, hurried to Fengxiang to join Emperor Suzong, and was made Reminder of the Left.
timeline/stages/2/events/2/summary: Du Fu gave up his post in Huazhou, took his family west to Qinzhou, and began his years of wandering.
timeline/stages/3/summary: Du Fu reached Chengdu and built a thatched cottage by Huanhua Creek, where he had a short spell of peace.
timeline/stages/3/events/0/summary: Du Fu built his thatched cottage by Huanhua Creek, lived on help from Yan Wu and others, and wrote many famous poems.
timeline/stages/4/summary: Du Fu went east down the Yangtze, stayed nearly two years in Kuizhou, and died of illness on the Xiang River.
timeline/stages/4/events/0/summary: Du Fu lived nearly two years in Kuizhou. His poems reached their peak here: the eight "Autumn Meditations" and "Climbing High".
timeline/stages/4/events/1/summary: Du Fu drifted between Tanzhou and Yueyang. He fell ill and died on a small boat, aged 59.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/2/panels/1/dia: Shadows move past the window. An old man climbs the wall and runs. An old woman goes out to meet them.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/2/panels/3/dia: Any men left in this house?!
Hide one more and the whole family dies!
events/759_qinzhou/phases/2/panels/4/dia: Three sons of mine went to guard Yecheng.
One sent a letter home. The other two have just been killed.
The living scrape by. The dead are gone for good…
There is no one left in the house — only a grandson still at the breast.
I am old and worn, but let me go with you tonight. If I hurry to the Heyang camp I can still cook the morning meal.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/2/panels/5/dia: I can't get out a single word.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/3/npcs/0/dialo: You are going to a place where men die. The pain twists inside me.
Better to leave a daughter by the roadside than marry her to a conscript.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/3/npcs/1/dialo: My village is wiped out. Near or far, it is all the same now.
If a man has no home to part from, what is left of being one of the people?
events/759_qinzhou/phases/3/npcs/2/dialo: My old wife lies in the road crying. The year is ending and her clothes are thin.
We both know this parting is for good — and still I worry that she is cold.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/4/options/0/re:
The post is small. I can't save them. But while I hold it I can spare one household.
(And every paper on this desk is taking someone away.)
events/759_qinzhou/phases/4/options/1/re:
I can't do this job any longer.
(He writes out his resignation and hands back the sash and the seal.)
events/759_qinzhou/phases/4/options/2/re: It goes up and sinks like a stone. I have done that once already.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/4/conclusion/n:
In the autumn of 759 Du Fu gave up his post at Huazhou and took his family west to Qinzhou.
It was the first time in his life — and the last — that he left office by his own choice.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/travelNarrat: West with the whole family. Walk it stop by stop.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/instruction: Click each stop and hear what happens on the road.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/waypoints/0/: I gave up the post, and I feel lighter.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/waypoints/1/: I thought we could settle here. But even our relatives have stopped answering.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/waypoints/2/: The Seven Songs of Tonggu — “There is a traveler, a traveler called Zimei, white hair uncombed, hanging past his ears.”
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/waypoints/3/: Somewhere you will have enough to eat.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/5/waypoints/4/: At the end of the winter of 759, Du Fu and his family walked into Chengdu.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/6/transitionTe:
Autumn went, winter came.
The family ate in the wind and slept in the open,
and came at last to the bank of Huanhua Creek.
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/6/que:
Complete this line from Zuo Si's "Rhapsody on the Wu Capital":
"Where formal robes made virtue visible, where high conduct arose. He founded a great enterprise on the highest virtue, and no age could ___ it."
events/747_exam/phases/2/questions/6/exp: From Zuo Si's "Rhapsody on the Wu Capital", praising the high character of Taibo of Wu and the bearing of Jizha of Yanling.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/1/prompt: The six panels of that night, shuffled. Put them back in the order things happened.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/1/panels/0/cap: By candlelight, the brush hasn't stopped
events/759_qinzhou/phases/1/panels/1/cap: Someone goes over the low wall
events/759_qinzhou/phases/1/panels/2/cap: The old woman opens the door, asking low
events/759_qinzhou/phases/1/panels/5/cap: The window is shut; he is listening
events/759_qinzhou/phases/1/revealNote:
The old man goes over the wall first, and only then does she open the door — this household has done this before.
Du Fu is writing in the first panel and listening in the last. That night he never went outside.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/3/instruction: Talk to all three people on the road.
events/759_qinzhou/phases/4/narrative: Du Fu is back in Huazhou, his desk piled with conscription papers. One brush. One blank sheet.
